To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRPV1-mediated responses in TRPA1-expressing neurons are modified by the presence of the TRPA1 channel.
TRPA1 channels modify TRPV1-mediated responses in DRG neurons.
the TRPV1 channel activities in TRPA1-negative neurons are faster than those in TRPA1 positive neurons, due to the TRPA1 channel-mediated current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrophysiological characteristics of TRPA1-positive DRG neurons and the role of TRPA1 channels in TRPV1-mediated nociceptive transmission.
the modulation of TRPV1 activity by TRPA1 activity in primary sensory neurons, which may be involved in the development of neuropathic pain.

the difference in the electrophysiological properties between TRPA1-sensitive and TRPA1-insensitive neurons, which is caused not by the difference in the expression levels of TRPV1 channels but the presence of TRPV1 and/or TRPA1 channels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRPA1 channel activation modifies the TRPV1-mediated electrophysiological currents in DRG neurons.
TRPA1 channels modify the responses induced by TRP channel agonists in primary sensory neurons.
the TRPV1-mediated inward current in TRPA 1-positive DRG is characterized by small current density and slow decay, which would result in a slow desensitization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPA1 channel modulates TRPV1-mediated electrophysiological response in primary sensory neurons.
the presence of TRPV1 in DRG neurons is not sufficient to induce the typical electrophysiological characteristics of TRPV1, but the co-existence of TRPA1 is necessary.
the TRPA1 channel modifies TRPV1 channel-mediated responses in sensory neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TRPA1 channels modify TRPV1-mediated responses, and that this modification is dependent on the intracellular Ca2+-level, which is a result of the TRPA1 channel activation.
the presence of TRPV1 and the TRPA1 channels in the same neuron modifies the electrophysiological response to the TRPV1 agonists, such as capsaicin.
TRPV1-mediated responses in TRPA1-expressing DRG neurons are different from those in TRPA1-nonexpressing DRG neurons.
